headline: Day three of the squeeze went global — KOSPI +4.4%, DAX at the top of its year — but Brent lost another 2.1% and bitcoin slipped again to 74,258: this rally is being financed by a weakening cycle, not confirmed by it.
summary: What changed overnight is geography, not quality. The US short-squeeze of 11/9 travelled: KOSPI +4.4% (still -20.9% on the month), TAIEX +2.5%, Nikkei +2.9% to 60,460, DAX +1.3% at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, Euro Stoxx +1.2%, CAC +1.1%. FX paid for it in the right places — USD/KRW -1.8%, EUR +0.7% to 1.1221, GBP +0.5%, AUD +0.6%, CEW turning up — even as DXY itself held 101.75 in the 87th percentile. Risk regime nudges to -10 from -11. That is the whole of the good news, and it is positioning, not fundamentals.

The cyclical tells went the other way. Brent -2.1% to 90.62, now -12.5% on the week and -13.5% on the month; WTI 85.37; RBOB -20.4% on the month at z=-1.90; DBC -1.8%. Copper is -5.1% on the month and the gold/silver ratio is +12.2% at z=1.80 — that is demand, not supply. Energy equities still refuse to mark it: XLE is only -4.8% on the month, +41.3% YTD and 5.6% above its 200-day, XOP -9.1% against crude's -13.5%. Cheap crude is disinflationary (5y breakevens 2.25, 16th percentile; 10y 2.22, 12th) and growth-negative at the same time — and the front end is only taking the second half of that message.

The invoice is unchanged and still accelerating. Investment-grade OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93, BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 with acceleration +0.86 — both 95th-96th percentile of the year and widening through a +2.3% S&P session. HY 3.42, +33bp on the month, 93rd percentile. Rates: 2-year 4.51 (+5bp), 5-year 4.64, 2s10s 32bp at the 22nd percentile, 3m10y -35bp on the month, 10-year real yield 2.63 in the 74th percentile, mortgage 7.18%. Meanwhile VIX sits at 19.98 and VIX/VIX3M at 0.9554, out of inversion — protection is cheap again precisely while high-grade credit deteriorates. Plumbing is thin underneath: RRP effectively empty at $0.25bn, reserves -2.1% over three months, net liquidity rolling over.

The two non-confirmations got worse, not better. Crypto refused a third straight up day: BTC -1.3% to 74,258, ETH -2.0% to 2,089 (-17.6% on the month), SOL -2.3% (-24.0%), COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its year, MSTR -18.6% on the month. And Brazil is still accelerating the wrong way on a soft-dollar day — USD/BRL 5.5296, +10.2% on the month at z=2.94 with acceleration 2.25, EWZ -25.1%, Bovespa acceleration -3.92 — against India compounding (INDA +11.7%, acceleration 2.76, USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91) and Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile. Beneath the bounce the regime hasn't moved: RSP/SPY z=3.59, growth/value at the 7th percentile, MTUM z=-3.01, NVDA -22.1% and GOOGL -18.1% on the month, versus HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%, LLY +19.7%. Rent the squeeze; own the rotation.

good.text: The bounce broadened across time zones overnight: KOSPI +4.4%, Nikkei +2.9% to 60,460, TAIEX +2.5%, DAX +1.3% at the very top of its 52-week range, Euro Stoxx +1.2%. Europe is now a trend, not a rental — DAX +6.1% on the month at z=1.13.

Bond volatility keeps repairing: MOVE 85.98, -14.3% on the week and -12.7% on the month, with the 10-year 42bp lower on the month at 4.86% and TLT +5.1%. Duration is no longer the source of the stress.

Dollar pressure eased exactly where it was hurting: USD/KRW -1.8%, EUR +0.7%, GBP +0.5%, AUD +0.6%, EM FX basket CEW turning up, USD/INR -3.0% on the month at z=-2.91. Asia's funding squeeze is loosening.
The rotation is real and still paying: equal-weight/cap-weight z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, SPW +3.7% on the month at the 95th percentile, XLV +10.3% (rel +14.1%), HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%.

The consumer is getting a tax cut from the pump: gasoline -20.4% on the month at z=-1.90, breakevens at 2.25/2.22 (16th/12th percentile), retail XRT +10.3% on the month and rel +14.1%. Labor is still intact — claims 189k at the lowest of the year, JOLTS +4.6%, unemployment 4.1%.

bad.text: High-grade credit is widening while stocks rally and accelerating as it does: IG OAS 0.93 (z=1.59, acc +0.93), BBB 1.16 (z=1.68, acc +0.86), both 95th-96th percentile; HY 3.42, +33bp on the month; HYG/IEF z=-1.66. This is the accelerating thing that is bad.

Crude broke again: Brent -2.1% to 90.62, -12.5% on the week, -13.5% on the month; WTI 85.37; DBC -1.8%. Energy equities have not marked it — XLE only -4.8% on the month, +41.3% YTD, 5.6% above its 200-day; XOP -9.1%.

The front end keeps tightening into a slowing cycle: 2-year 4.51 (+5bp), 2s10s 32bp at the 22nd percentile, 3m10y -35bp on the month, 10-year real yield 2.63 in the 74th percentile, 30-year mortgage 7.18% at the 85th percentile.

Crypto refused the global squeeze for a third session: BTC -1.3% to 74,258, ETH -2.0% (-17.6% 1m), SOL -2.3% (-24.0%), COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its year, MSTR -18.6% on the month. The liquidity beta is absent.
Brazil is the one thing accelerating the wrong way while EM FX turns up: USD/BRL 5.5296, +10.2% on the month at z=2.94 with acceleration 2.25, EWZ -25.1%, Bovespa acceleration -3.92.

Under the squeeze the leadership is still broken: NVDA -22.1% and GOOGL -18.1% on the month (z=-2.39), SMH/SPY z=-2.70, MTUM z=-3.01, growth/value at the 7th percentile. A 7% day in semis does not undo a -16.4% month of relative loss.

trades.name: Long IEF vs short LQD — high grade is widening into the rally
trades.line: Long IEF / short LQD: IG and BBB spreads widening at z=1.6+
trades.expr: Equal dollars long IEF against short LQD; both legs liquid, the pair isolates investment-grade spread from duration. Roll monthly.
trades.thesis: LQD's +2.2% month is entirely duration — IG OAS went from 0.82 to 0.93 and BBB from 1.02 to 1.16 in the same window. Owning Treasuries against corporates captures the one deterioration that has not reversed on any up day.
trades.trigger: IG OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93 and BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 with acceleration +0.86, 95th-96th percentile of the year, both still widening through a +2.3% S&P session while VIX sits at 19.98.
trades.stop: IG OAS back under 0.85 and BBB acceleration flipping negative for a week — that means the squeeze reached real credit.
trades.target: IG OAS toward 1.10 / BBB 1.35, roughly 4% on the pair.

trades.name: Short XOP — energy equities still haven't marked crude
trades.line: Short XOP: Brent -13.5% on the month, XLE still +41% YTD
trades.expr: Short XOP outright or buy Jan XOP puts; optionally beta-hedge a third of the notional with long SPY. OIH is the higher-beta version of the same idea.
trades.thesis: Crude is down 13.5% on the month and gasoline 20.4%, yet the equity complex trades like $100 oil: XLE is 5.6% above its 200-day and +41.3% YTD. Either crude reverses hard or E&P earnings estimates come down.
trades.trigger: Brent -2.1% overnight to 90.62 and -12.5% on the week; RBOB at z=-1.90; XOP only -9.1% on the month with 1m relative strength -5.9% and rolling over; XOM -0.7% and CVX -0.9% on a +2.3% tape was the first leak.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 96 and XOP relative strength turns up — stop the position at -8%.
trades.target: XOP down another 12% toward the crude-implied level.

trades.name: Short SMH vs long XLV — rent the squeeze, don't marry it
trades.line: Short SMH / long XLV: semis squeezed, leadership still broken
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral: short SMH against long XLV. Express the short as SMH puts if you want defined risk through earnings.
trades.thesis: The squeeze lifted the most damaged names on no new information while the index's biggest stock fell. Healthcare is the opposite: trend up, relative strength up, extended for the right reasons.
trades.trigger: SOXX +7.5% and SMH +5.1% on 11/9 with NVDA -4.3% the same day (-22.1% on the month, 12.6% below its 200-day, 19th percentile); SMH/SPY still z=-2.70 and -16.4% relative over a month. XLV +10.3% on the month at z=2.40, relative +14.1%, LLY +19.7%.
trades.stop: NVDA reclaims its 200-day and SMH/SPY trend flips to up — pair stop at -7%.
trades.target: +10% on the pair as semis give back the squeeze and XLV keeps compounding.

trades.name: Long India vs short Brazil — EM dispersion, not EM beta
trades.line: Long INDA / short EWZ while BRL breaks at z=2.9
trades.expr: Equal dollars long INDA against short EWZ. The FX purist version is long USD/BRL outright; the equity pair carries less carry cost.
trades.thesis: EM is not one trade. India has compounding flows and a strengthening currency; Brazil has a currency in a disorderly move and an index whose acceleration is the worst in the digest.
trades.trigger: USD/BRL +0.5% today to 5.5296, +10.2% on the month at z=2.94 with acceleration 2.25 — on a session when CEW turned up and KRW rallied 1.8%. EWZ -25.1% on the month with acceleration -3.39 vs INDA +11.7% with acceleration 2.76 and USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back under 5.25 with Bovespa acceleration positive — close at -7%.

trades.name: Short ETH — the liquidity beta never showed up
trades.line: Short ETH: no bid in a three-day global squeeze
trades.expr: Short ETH spot or perp; the cleaner cross is short ETH against long BTC (ETH/BTC -7.1% on the month, 23rd percentile). Size small, this is high-vol.
trades.thesis: When Korea rips 4.4% and European indices print highs and the most liquidity-sensitive asset in the world goes down, there is no marginal dollar. Reserves -2.1% over three months and RRP at $0.25bn say the same thing.
trades.trigger: ETH -2.0% overnight to 2,089 and -17.6% on the month; SOL -2.3% and -24.0%; BTC -1.3% to 74,258 on day three of the squeeze; COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its year, MSTR -18.6% on the month.
trades.stop: BTC back above 80,000 with ETH/BTC turning up — cover at -12%.

trades.name: Long SPLV vs short SPHB — beta is still being de-rated
trades.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB: high-beta down 18.6% vs low-vol in 1m
trades.expr: Equal dollars long SPLV against short SPHB. Add a 1-2% notional SPY Dec put spread while VIX/VIX3M is back at 0.9554 and protection is cheap.
trades.thesis: The regime shift from high beta to quality cash flows has run for a month with acceleration behind it; a one-day +4.2% pop in the ratio is a rental inside a downtrend, and it happened while BBB spreads widened.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV -18.6% on the month at z=-2.91 with acceleration -2.62, 6.7% below its 200-day; SPLV z=2.23 with acceleration 2.03 at the 93rd percentile; VIX/VIX3M out of inversion at 0.9554 while IG and BBB accelerate wider.

trades.name: Long GDX vs short GLD — miners over metal
trades.line: Long GDX / short GLD: miners/gold at 88th pctile, acc +1.05
trades.expr: Equal dollars long GDX against short GLD, which strips the bullion move and keeps the operating leverage. GDXJ for the higher-beta version.
trades.thesis: Gold is consolidating (-3.2% on the month, -9.2% below its 200-day) while the equities are discounting margin at $4,000 bullion. The ratio is making new highs against a falling metal — that is the signature of real earnings, not a hedge bid.
trades.trigger: GDX +15.6% on the week and +4.4% on 11/9 with gold -0.8% today; GDX/GOLD +10.1% on the week, acceleration 1.05, 88th percentile of the year; NEM +14.7% on the week with relative strength +9.9%.
trades.stop: Gold breaks 3,900 and miners lead it down — ratio rolls over, stop at -8%.
